key_insight: A mean-flow-based reduced-order modeling framework can capture turbulent channel-flow statistics more faithfully by explicitly incorporating Reynolds-stress effects into the Galerkin projection.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate surrogate modeling route for turbulent CFD, improving short-time prediction and statistical reconstruction from a low-dimensional basis.
method: Linearize around the turbulent mean flow and build modal bases from controllability/observability Gramians or balanced truncation.
Modify the Galerkin projection to account for the divergence of Reynolds stresses using knowledge of the mean flow.
Compare the resulting ROM against POD-Galerkin and other linearization-based bases for both statistics and forecasting.
evidence_signal: In a minimal channel DNS at Re_tau ≈ 185, the framework reproduces turbulence statistics comparable to the reference and gives short-time velocity-field reconstructions, with balanced truncation outperforming controllability modes.
watch_item: The approach depends on an accurate mean flow and careful treatment of Reynolds-stress projection, which may become more challenging as Reynolds number and flow complexity increase.
paper_title: Mean-flow-based reduced-order models of turbulent channel flow
